CHAPTER V

PROTECTION OF VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

To realize such integrity and harmony, it is highly dependent on each person within the scope of the household, especially the level of quality of behavior and self-control of each person within the scope of the household. The integrity and harmony of the household can be disrupted if quality and self-control cannot be controlled, which ultimately can result in domestic violence resulting in insecurity or injustice against people within the scope of the household. To prevent, protect victims, and prosecute perpetrators of domestic violence, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and prosecution of perpetrators in accordance with the philosophy of Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state views that all forms of violence, especially domestic violence, are violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of discrimination. The state's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, together with its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to protection of his/her person, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and shall have the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something that is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to obtain facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice". Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence, and domestic neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate domestic violence. The Regional Regulation regulates the matter of prevention and protection as well as recovery for victims of violence, and regulates the obligations of law enforcement officials, health workers, social workers, assisting volunteers, or spiritual counselors to protect victims so that they are more sensitive and responsive to the interests of the household which from the outset is directed at the integrity and harmony of the household. To prevent domestic violence, the Regional Government is obliged to carry out duties in the field of women's empowerment to carry out preventive actions, among others, organizing communication, information, and education regarding the prevention of violence against women and children. Based on these considerations, it is time to establish a Regional Regulation that is regulated comprehensively, clearly, and firmly in the implementation of protection of women and children including protection of women and children victims of violence. I. GENERAL

The existence of Regional Regulations that side with vulnerable or subordinated groups, particularly women and children, becomes very necessary in connection with the many social problems that result in the deprivation of the human rights of women and children. The human rights of women and children are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child as well as the ratification of the convention on the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, however the enforcement of the human rights of women and children has still not been able to encourage becoming a political commitment in the Region. The form of implementation of protection of women carried out by the Government is to implement gender mainstreaming, namely a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of regional development program policies within the framework of National development. A child is a mandate as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because in him/her is inherent dignity, honor, and rights as a human being that must be upheld. From the perspective of the life of the nation and state, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms. Although Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection has included the rights of children, the implementation of the obligations and responsibilities of parents, family, community, government, and the state to provide protection to children, a Regional Regulation is still needed as a juridical foundation for the implementation of such obligations and responsibilities in the Region. Thus, the establishment of this Regional Regulation is based on the consideration that child protection in all its aspects is part of development activities in the Region, particularly in advancing the life of the nation and state. Parents, family, and community are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise, in the context of implementing child protection, the state and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their growth and development in an optimal and directed manner. This Regional Regulation affirms that the accountability of parents, family, community, Regional Government and the state is a series of activities carried out continuously for the protection of children's rights. This series of activities must be sustainable and directed to ensure the growth and development of children, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially. This action is intended to realize the best life for children who are expected to be potential successors to the nation, resilient, having nationalism imbued with noble character and Pancasila values, as well as having a strong will to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. Child protection efforts need to be implemented as early as possible, namely from the fetus in the womb until the child is 18 (eighteen) years old. Starting from the concept of holistic, comprehensive, and complete child protection, this Regional Regulation places the obligation to provide protection to children based on the following principles:

a. non-discrimination; b. the best interests of the child; c. the right to life, survival, and development; and d. respect for the views of the child. In conducting guidance, development and protection of children, the role of the community is needed, whether through child protection institutions, religious institutions, non-governmental organizations, community organizations, social organizations, business world, mass media, or educational institutions. The form of implementation of child protection carried out by the Regional Government is through mainstreaming children's rights, namely integrating children's issues and rights into every stage of development which includes planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of laws and regulations, policy programs and budgets with the principles of the best interests of the child. The integrity and harmony of a happy, safe, peaceful, and tranquil household is the aspiration of every person in the household. The Republic of Indonesia is a state based on the Belief in the One and Only God as guaranteed by Article 29 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Thus, every person within the scope of the household in carrying out their rights and obligations must be based on religion. This needs to be continuously developed in order to build household integrity.

20. Foster child is a child who is cared for by a person or institution, to be given guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health, because their parents or one of their parents is unable to ensure the child's proper growth and development.

21. Custody is the power of parents to care for, educate, maintain, nurture, protect, and develop children in accordance with their religion and abilities, talents, and interests.

22. Child rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, society, government, and the state.

23. Society is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 24. Companion is a social worker who has professional competence in their field.

25. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and their children, or mother and their children, or blood relatives in direct line upwards or downwards up to the third degree.

26. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.

27. Guardian is a person or body that in fact exercises custody as a parent to a child.

28. Every person is an individual or corporation. 29. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children (PPTPA) is a cooperative network that carries out integrated service functions for the protection of women and children victims of violence.

30. Safe House (Shelter) is a shelter for women and children including family and witnesses who are victims of violence.

31. Community Social Institution is a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) and/or other community organization.

32. Human Trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over the other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.

33. Criminal Act of Human Trafficking is any act or series of acts that meet the elements of a criminal act specified in the Law on Human Trafficking.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

The existence of Regional Regulations that side with vulnerable or subordinated groups, particularly women and children, becomes very necessary in connection with the many social problems that result in the deprivation of the human rights of women and children. The human rights of women and children are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child as well as the ratification of the convention on the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, however the enforcement of the human rights of women and children has still not been able to encourage becoming a political commitment in the Region. The form of implementation of protection of women carried out by the Government is to implement gender mainstreaming, namely a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of regional development program policies within the framework of National development. A child is a mandate as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because in him/her is inherent dignity, honor, and rights as a human being that must be upheld. From the perspective of the life of the nation and state, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms. Although Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection has included the rights of children, the implementation of the obligations and responsibilities of parents, family, community, government, and the state to provide protection to children, a Regional Regulation is still needed as a juridical foundation for the implementation of such obligations and responsibilities in the Region. Thus, the establishment of this Regional Regulation is based on the consideration that child protection in all its aspects is part of development activities in the Region, particularly in advancing the life of the nation and state. Parents, family, and community are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise, in the context of implementing child protection, the state and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their growth and development in an optimal and directed manner. This Regional Regulation affirms that the accountability of parents, family, community, Regional Government and the state is a series of activities carried out continuously for the protection of children's rights. This series of activities must be sustainable and directed to ensure the growth and development of children, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially. This action is intended to realize the best life for children who are expected to be potential successors to the nation, resilient, having nationalism imbued with noble character and Pancasila values, as well as having a strong will to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. Child protection efforts need to be implemented as early as possible, namely from the fetus in the womb until the child is 18 (eighteen) years old. Starting from the concept of holistic, comprehensive, and complete child protection, this Regional Regulation places the obligation to provide protection to children based on the following principles:

a. non-discrimination; b. the best interests of the child; c. the right to life, survival, and development; and d. respect for the views of the child. In conducting guidance, development and protection of children, the role of the community is needed, whether through child protection institutions, religious institutions, non-governmental organizations, community organizations, social organizations, business world, mass media, or educational institutions. The form of implementation of child protection carried out by the Regional Government is through mainstreaming children's rights, namely integrating children's issues and rights into every stage of development which includes planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of laws and regulations, policy programs and budgets with the principles of the best interests of the child. The integrity and harmony of a happy, safe, peaceful, and tranquil household is the aspiration of every person in the household. The Republic of Indonesia is a state based on the Belief in the One and Only God as guaranteed by Article 29 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Thus, every person within the scope of the household in carrying out their rights and obligations must be based on religion. This needs to be continuously developed in order to build household integrity.

Article 3

The objectives of implementing the protection of women are: a. to ensure the fulfillment of women's rights;

b. to protect women and prevent all forms of violence and discrimination against women; and

c. to maintain the integrity of a harmonious and prosperous household.

Part Four

Implementation of Protection

Article 7

Regional Government is obliged to implement efforts for the protection of women.

To realize such integrity and harmony, it is highly dependent on each person within the scope of the household, especially the level of quality of behavior and self-control of each person within the scope of the household. The integrity and harmony of the household can be disrupted if quality and self-control cannot be controlled, which ultimately can result in domestic violence resulting in insecurity or injustice against people within the scope of the household. To prevent, protect victims, and prosecute perpetrators of domestic violence, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and prosecution of perpetrators in accordance with the philosophy of Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state views that all forms of violence, especially domestic violence, are violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of discrimination. The state's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, together with its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to protection of his/her person, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and shall have the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something that is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to obtain facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice". Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence, and domestic neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate domestic violence. The Regional Regulation regulates the matter of prevention and protection as well as recovery for victims of violence, and regulates the obligations of law enforcement officials, health workers, social workers, assisting volunteers, or spiritual counselors to protect victims so that they are more sensitive and responsive to the interests of the household which from the outset is directed at the integrity and harmony of the household. To prevent domestic violence, the Regional Government is obliged to carry out duties in the field of women's empowerment to carry out preventive actions, among others, organizing communication, information, and education regarding the prevention of violence against women and children. Based on these considerations, it is time to establish a Regional Regulation that is regulated comprehensively, clearly, and firmly in the implementation of protection of women and children including protection of women and children victims of violence. II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 64

(1) Families and communities are obliged to prevent the occurrence of violence and the occurrence of criminal acts against women and children.

(2) Every person who hears, sees, or knows of the occurrence of violence is obliged to make efforts in accordance with their capacity to:

a. prevent the continuation of criminal acts;
b. provide protection to victims;
c. provide emergency assistance; and
d. assist in the process of filing an application for protection order.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Region is Trenggalek Regency.

2. Regional Government is the Government of Trenggalek Regency.

3. Regent is the Regent of Trenggalek.

4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of Trenggalek Regency.

5. Implementation is the form of execution of protection of women and children including protection of women and children victims of violence.

6. Protection of Women is any effort made by family, government and others aimed at women to ensure the fulfillment of women's rights as a form of respect for human rights.

7. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.

8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences violence and/or threat of violence.

9. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully.

10. Child Protection is all activities to ensure and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.

11. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child who is still in the womb.

12. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of abuse of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic substances, and other addictive substances (drugs), children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of abuse and neglect.

13. Protection of Women and Children Victims of violence is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, family, advocates, police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against Women and Children will or has occurred.

14. Gender mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of national development program policies.

15. Child rights mainstreaming is a strategy to integrate child issues and rights into every stage of development which includes planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of Laws and Regulations, policies, programs, activities and budgets with the principles of the best interests of the child.

16. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social.

17. Child with disability is a child who experiences physical and/or mental obstacles that interfere with their growth and development properly.

18. Child with excellence is a child who has extraordinary intelligence, or has special potential and/or talent.

19. Adopted child is a child whose rights are transferred from the environment of the authority of the family of parents, legal guardian, or other person responsible for the care, education, and raising of the child, into the family environment of adoptive parents based on a court decision or determination.

20. Foster child is a child who is cared for by a person or institution, to be given guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health, because their parents or one of their parents is unable to ensure the child's proper growth and development.

21. Custody is the power of parents to care for, educate, maintain, nurture, protect, and develop children in accordance with their religion and abilities, talents, and interests.

22. Child rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, society, government, and the state.

23. Society is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 24. Companion is a social worker who has professional competence in their field.

25. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and their children, or mother and their children, or blood relatives in direct line upwards or downwards up to the third degree.

26. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.

27. Guardian is a person or body that in fact exercises custody as a parent to a child.

28. Every person is an individual or corporation. 29. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children (PPTPA) is a cooperative network that carries out integrated service functions for the protection of women and children victims of violence.

30. Safe House (Shelter) is a shelter for women and children including family and witnesses who are victims of violence.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

The existence of Regional Regulations that side with vulnerable or subordinated groups, particularly women and children, becomes very necessary in connection with the many social problems that result in the deprivation of the human rights of women and children. The human rights of women and children are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child as well as the ratification of the convention on the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, however the enforcement of the human rights of women and children has still not been able to encourage becoming a political commitment in the Region. The form of implementation of protection of women carried out by the Government is to implement gender mainstreaming, namely a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of regional development program policies within the framework of National development. A child is a mandate as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because in him/her is inherent dignity, honor, and rights as a human being that must be upheld. From the perspective of the life of the nation and state, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms. Although Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection has included the rights of children, the implementation of the obligations and responsibilities of parents, family, community, government, and the state to provide protection to children, a Regional Regulation is still needed as a juridical foundation for the implementation of such obligations and responsibilities in the Region. Thus, the establishment of this Regional Regulation is based on the consideration that child protection in all its aspects is part of development activities in the Region, particularly in advancing the life of the nation and state. Parents, family, and community are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise, in the context of implementing child protection, the state and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their growth and development in an optimal and directed manner. This Regional Regulation affirms that the accountability of parents, family, community, Regional Government and the state is a series of activities carried out continuously for the protection of children's rights. This series of activities must be sustainable and directed to ensure the growth and development of children, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially. This action is intended to realize the best life for children who are expected to be potential successors to the nation, resilient, having nationalism imbued with noble character and Pancasila values, as well as having a strong will to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. Child protection efforts need to be implemented as early as possible, namely from the fetus in the womb until the child is 18 (eighteen) years old. Starting from the concept of holistic, comprehensive, and complete child protection, this Regional Regulation places the obligation to provide protection to children based on the following principles:

a. non-discrimination; b. the best interests of the child; c. the right to life, survival, and development; and d. respect for the views of the child. In conducting guidance, development and protection of children, the role of the community is needed, whether through child protection institutions, religious institutions, non-governmental organizations, community organizations, social organizations, business world, mass media, or educational institutions. The form of implementation of child protection carried out by the Regional Government is through mainstreaming children's rights, namely integrating children's issues and rights into every stage of development which includes planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of laws and regulations, policy programs and budgets with the principles of the best interests of the child. The integrity and harmony of a happy, safe, peaceful, and tranquil household is the aspiration of every person in the household. The Republic of Indonesia is a state based on the Belief in the One and Only God as guaranteed by Article 29 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Thus, every person within the scope of the household in carrying out their rights and obligations must be based on religion. This needs to be continuously developed in order to build household integrity.

Article 51

(1) Special protection for children who are exploited economically and/or sexually as referred to in Article 44 is the obligation and responsibility of the Regional Government and society.

(2) Special protection for children who are exploited as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through: a. dissemination and/or socialization of provisions of Laws and Regulations relating to the protection of children who are exploited economically and/or sexually;

b. monitoring, reporting, and imposition of sanctions; and c. involvement of various Regional Government agencies, companies, labor unions, Social Community Institutions, and the community in the elimination of exploitation of children economically and/or sexually.

(3) Every person is prohibited from placing, allowing, committing, ordering to commit, or participating in the exploitation of children as referred to in paragraph (1).

Article 4

The objectives of implementing child protection are: a. to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity;

b. to protect children and prevent all forms of violence and discrimination against children; and

c. to create quality children who have noble character and are prosperous.

Article 29

(1) The Regional Government is obligated to provide facilities and organize comprehensive health efforts for children, so that every child obtains optimal health status from the womb.

(3) Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) include promotive, preventive, curative, and rehabilitative efforts, both for basic health services and referrals.

To realize such integrity and harmony, it is highly dependent on each person within the scope of the household, especially the level of quality of behavior and self-control of each person within the scope of the household. The integrity and harmony of the household can be disrupted if quality and self-control cannot be controlled, which ultimately can result in domestic violence resulting in insecurity or injustice against people within the scope of the household. To prevent, protect victims, and prosecute perpetrators of domestic violence, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and prosecution of perpetrators in accordance with the philosophy of Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state views that all forms of violence, especially domestic violence, are violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of discrimination. The state's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, together with its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to protection of his/her person, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and shall have the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something that is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to obtain facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice". Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence, and domestic neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate domestic violence. The Regional Regulation regulates the matter of prevention and protection as well as recovery for victims of violence, and regulates the obligations of law enforcement officials, health workers, social workers, assisting volunteers, or spiritual counselors to protect victims so that they are more sensitive and responsive to the interests of the household which from the outset is directed at the integrity and harmony of the household. To prevent domestic violence, the Regional Government is obliged to carry out duties in the field of women's empowerment to carry out preventive actions, among others, organizing communication, information, and education regarding the prevention of violence against women and children. Based on these considerations, it is time to establish a Regional Regulation that is regulated comprehensively, clearly, and firmly in the implementation of protection of women and children including protection of women and children victims of violence. 7. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.

8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences violence and/or threat of violence.

9. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully.

10. Child Protection is all activities to ensure and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.

21. Custody is the power of parents to care for, educate, maintain, nurture, protect, and develop children in accordance with their religion and abilities, talents, and interests.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

The existence of Regional Regulations that side with vulnerable or subordinated groups, particularly women and children, becomes very necessary in connection with the many social problems that result in the deprivation of the human rights of women and children. The human rights of women and children are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child as well as the ratification of the convention on the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, however the enforcement of the human rights of women and children has still not been able to encourage becoming a political commitment in the Region. The form of implementation of protection of women carried out by the Government is to implement gender mainstreaming, namely a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of regional development program policies within the framework of National development. A child is a mandate as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because in him/her is inherent dignity, honor, and rights as a human being that must be upheld. From the perspective of the life of the nation and state, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms. Although Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection has included the rights of children, the implementation of the obligations and responsibilities of parents, family, community, government, and the state to provide protection to children, a Regional Regulation is still needed as a juridical foundation for the implementation of such obligations and responsibilities in the Region. Thus, the establishment of this Regional Regulation is based on the consideration that child protection in all its aspects is part of development activities in the Region, particularly in advancing the life of the nation and state. Parents, family, and community are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise, in the context of implementing child protection, the state and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their growth and development in an optimal and directed manner. This Regional Regulation affirms that the accountability of parents, family, community, Regional Government and the state is a series of activities carried out continuously for the protection of children's rights. This series of activities must be sustainable and directed to ensure the growth and development of children, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially. This action is intended to realize the best life for children who are expected to be potential successors to the nation, resilient, having nationalism imbued with noble character and Pancasila values, as well as having a strong will to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. Child protection efforts need to be implemented as early as possible, namely from the fetus in the womb until the child is 18 (eighteen) years old. Starting from the concept of holistic, comprehensive, and complete child protection, this Regional Regulation places the obligation to provide protection to children based on the following principles:

a. non-discrimination; b. the best interests of the child; c. the right to life, survival, and development; and d. respect for the views of the child. In conducting guidance, development and protection of children, the role of the community is needed, whether through child protection institutions, religious institutions, non-governmental organizations, community organizations, social organizations, business world, mass media, or educational institutions. The form of implementation of child protection carried out by the Regional Government is through mainstreaming children's rights, namely integrating children's issues and rights into every stage of development which includes planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of laws and regulations, policy programs and budgets with the principles of the best interests of the child. The integrity and harmony of a happy, safe, peaceful, and tranquil household is the aspiration of every person in the household. The Republic of Indonesia is a state based on the Belief in the One and Only God as guaranteed by Article 29 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Thus, every person within the scope of the household in carrying out their rights and obligations must be based on religion. This needs to be continuously developed in order to build household integrity.

Part Five

To realize such integrity and harmony, it is highly dependent on each person within the scope of the household, especially the level of quality of behavior and self-control of each person within the scope of the household. The integrity and harmony of the household can be disrupted if quality and self-control cannot be controlled, which ultimately can result in domestic violence resulting in insecurity or injustice against people within the scope of the household. To prevent, protect victims, and prosecute perpetrators of domestic violence, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and prosecution of perpetrators in accordance with the philosophy of Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state views that all forms of violence, especially domestic violence, are violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of discrimination. The state's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, together with its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to protection of his/her person, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and shall have the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something that is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to obtain facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice". Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence, and domestic neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate domestic violence. The Regional Regulation regulates the matter of prevention and protection as well as recovery for victims of violence, and regulates the obligations of law enforcement officials, health workers, social workers, assisting volunteers, or spiritual counselors to protect victims so that they are more sensitive and responsive to the interests of the household which from the outset is directed at the integrity and harmony of the household. To prevent domestic violence, the Regional Government is obliged to carry out duties in the field of women's empowerment to carry out preventive actions, among others, organizing communication, information, and education regarding the prevention of violence against women and children. Based on these considerations, it is time to establish a Regional Regulation that is regulated comprehensively, clearly, and firmly in the implementation of protection of women and children including protection of women and children victims of violence. To realize such integrity and harmony, it is highly dependent on each person within the scope of the household, especially the level of quality of behavior and self-control of each person within the scope of the household. The integrity and harmony of the household can be disrupted if quality and self-control cannot be controlled, which ultimately can result in domestic violence resulting in insecurity or injustice against people within the scope of the household. To prevent, protect victims, and prosecute perpetrators of domestic violence, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and prosecution of perpetrators in accordance with the philosophy of Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state views that all forms of violence, especially domestic violence, are violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of discrimination. The state's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, together with its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to protection of his/her person, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and shall have the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something that is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to obtain facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice". Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence, and domestic neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate domestic violence. The Regional Regulation regulates the matter of prevention and protection as well as recovery for victims of violence, and regulates the obligations of law enforcement officials, health workers, social workers, assisting volunteers, or spiritual counselors to protect victims so that they are more sensitive and responsive to the interests of the household which from the outset is directed at the integrity and harmony of the household. To prevent domestic violence, the Regional Government is obliged to carry out duties in the field of women's empowerment to carry out preventive actions, among others, organizing communication, information, and education regarding the prevention of violence against women and children. Based on these considerations, it is time to establish a Regional Regulation that is regulated comprehensively, clearly, and firmly in the implementation of protection of women and children including protection of women and children victims of violence. I. GENERAL

The existence of Regional Regulations that side with vulnerable or subordinated groups, particularly women and children, becomes very necessary in connection with the many social problems that result in the deprivation of the human rights of women and children. The human rights of women and children are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child as well as the ratification of the convention on the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, however the enforcement of the human rights of women and children has still not been able to encourage becoming a political commitment in the Region. The form of implementation of protection of women carried out by the Government is to implement gender mainstreaming, namely a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of regional development program policies within the framework of National development. A child is a mandate as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because in him/her is inherent dignity, honor, and rights as a human being that must be upheld. From the perspective of the life of the nation and state, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms. Although Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection has included the rights of children, the implementation of the obligations and responsibilities of parents, family, community, government, and the state to provide protection to children, a Regional Regulation is still needed as a juridical foundation for the implementation of such obligations and responsibilities in the Region. Thus, the establishment of this Regional Regulation is based on the consideration that child protection in all its aspects is part of development activities in the Region, particularly in advancing the life of the nation and state. Parents, family, and community are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise, in the context of implementing child protection, the state and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their growth and development in an optimal and directed manner. This Regional Regulation affirms that the accountability of parents, family, community, Regional Government and the state is a series of activities carried out continuously for the protection of children's rights. This series of activities must be sustainable and directed to ensure the growth and development of children, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially. This action is intended to realize the best life for children who are expected to be potential successors to the nation, resilient, having nationalism imbued with noble character and Pancasila values, as well as having a strong will to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. Child protection efforts need to be implemented as early as possible, namely from the fetus in the womb until the child is 18 (eighteen) years old. Starting from the concept of holistic, comprehensive, and complete child protection, this Regional Regulation places the obligation to provide protection to children based on the following principles:

a. non-discrimination; b. the best interests of the child; c. the right to life, survival, and development; and d. respect for the views of the child. In conducting guidance, development and protection of children, the role of the community is needed, whether through child protection institutions, religious institutions, non-governmental organizations, community organizations, social organizations, business world, mass media, or educational institutions. The form of implementation of child protection carried out by the Regional Government is through mainstreaming children's rights, namely integrating children's issues and rights into every stage of development which includes planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of laws and regulations, policy programs and budgets with the principles of the best interests of the child. The integrity and harmony of a happy, safe, peaceful, and tranquil household is the aspiration of every person in the household. The Republic of Indonesia is a state based on the Belief in the One and Only God as guaranteed by Article 29 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Thus, every person within the scope of the household in carrying out their rights and obligations must be based on religion. This needs to be continuously developed in order to build household integrity.

Human Trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over the other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.

33. Criminal Act of Human Trafficking is any act or series of acts that meet the elements of a criminal act specified in the Law on Human Trafficking.

Article 65

(1) The community participates in assisting prevention and handling efforts for victims of violence and criminal acts against women and children.

(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be realized through actions of providing information and/or reporting the occurrence of violence and criminal acts against women and children to law enforcement or the authorities, or participating in handling victims of violence and criminal acts against women and children.

(3) To carry out the participation as referred to in paragraph (2), the community is entitled to legal protection.

(4) The Regional Government in organizing victim protection may cooperate with the community or social community organizations.

Article 64

(1) Families and communities are obliged to prevent the occurrence of violence and the occurrence of criminal acts against women and children.

(2) Every person who hears, sees, or knows of the occurrence of violence is obliged to make efforts in accordance with their capacity to:

a. prevent the continuation of criminal acts;
b. provide protection to victims;
c. provide emergency assistance; and
d. assist in the process of filing an application for protection order.

To realize such integrity and harmony, it is highly dependent on each person within the scope of the household, especially the level of quality of behavior and self-control of each person within the scope of the household. The integrity and harmony of the household can be disrupted if quality and self-control cannot be controlled, which ultimately can result in domestic violence resulting in insecurity or injustice against people within the scope of the household. To prevent, protect victims, and prosecute perpetrators of domestic violence, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and prosecution of perpetrators in accordance with the philosophy of Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state views that all forms of violence, especially domestic violence, are violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of discrimination. The state's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, together with its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to protection of his/her person, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and shall have the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something that is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to obtain facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice". Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence, and domestic neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate domestic violence. The Regional Regulation regulates the matter of prevention and protection as well as recovery for victims of violence, and regulates the obligations of law enforcement officials, health workers, social workers, assisting volunteers, or spiritual counselors to protect victims so that they are more sensitive and responsive to the interests of the household which from the outset is directed at the integrity and harmony of the household. To prevent domestic violence, the Regional Government is obliged to carry out duties in the field of women's empowerment to carry out preventive actions, among others, organizing communication, information, and education regarding the prevention of violence against women and children. Based on these considerations, it is time to establish a Regional Regulation that is regulated comprehensively, clearly, and firmly in the implementation of protection of women and children including protection of women and children victims of violence. I. GENERAL

The existence of Regional Regulations that side with vulnerable or subordinated groups, particularly women and children, becomes very necessary in connection with the many social problems that result in the deprivation of the human rights of women and children. The human rights of women and children are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child as well as the ratification of the convention on the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, however the enforcement of the human rights of women and children has still not been able to encourage becoming a political commitment in the Region. The form of implementation of protection of women carried out by the Government is to implement gender mainstreaming, namely a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of regional development program policies within the framework of National development. A child is a mandate as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because in him/her is inherent dignity, honor, and rights as a human being that must be upheld. From the perspective of the life of the nation and state, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms. Although Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection has included the rights of children, the implementation of the obligations and responsibilities of parents, family, community, government, and the state to provide protection to children, a Regional Regulation is still needed as a juridical foundation for the implementation of such obligations and responsibilities in the Region. Thus, the establishment of this Regional Regulation is based on the consideration that child protection in all its aspects is part of development activities in the Region, particularly in advancing the life of the nation and state. Parents, family, and community are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise, in the context of implementing child protection, the state and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their growth and development in an optimal and directed manner. This Regional Regulation affirms that the accountability of parents, family, community, Regional Government and the state is a series of activities carried out continuously for the protection of children's rights. This series of activities must be sustainable and directed to ensure the growth and development of children, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially. This action is intended to realize the best life for children who are expected to be potential successors to the nation, resilient, having nationalism imbued with noble character and Pancasila values, as well as having a strong will to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. Child protection efforts need to be implemented as early as possible, namely from the fetus in the womb until the child is 18 (eighteen) years old. Starting from the concept of holistic, comprehensive, and complete child protection, this Regional Regulation places the obligation to provide protection to children based on the following principles:

a. non-discrimination; b. the best interests of the child; c. the right to life, survival, and development; and d. respect for the views of the child. In conducting guidance, development and protection of children, the role of the community is needed, whether through child protection institutions, religious institutions, non-governmental organizations, community organizations, social organizations, business world, mass media, or educational institutions. The form of implementation of child protection carried out by the Regional Government is through mainstreaming children's rights, namely integrating children's issues and rights into every stage of development which includes planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of laws and regulations, policy programs and budgets with the principles of the best interests of the child. The integrity and harmony of a happy, safe, peaceful, and tranquil household is the aspiration of every person in the household. The Republic of Indonesia is a state based on the Belief in the One and Only God as guaranteed by Article 29 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Thus, every person within the scope of the household in carrying out their rights and obligations must be based on religion. This needs to be continuously developed in order to build household integrity.

3.8.text: To realize such integrity and harmony, it is highly dependent on each person within the scope of the household, especially the level of quality of behavior and self-control of each person within the scope of the household. The integrity and harmony of the household can be disrupted if quality and self-control cannot be controlled, which ultimately can result in domestic violence resulting in insecurity or injustice against people within the scope of the household. To prevent, protect victims, and prosecute perpetrators of domestic violence, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and prosecution of perpetrators in accordance with the philosophy of Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state views that all forms of violence, especially domestic violence, are violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of discrimination. The state's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, together with its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to protection of his/her person, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and shall have the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something that is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to obtain facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice". Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence, and domestic neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate domestic violence. The Regional Regulation regulates the matter of prevention and protection as well as recovery for victims of violence, and regulates the obligations of law enforcement officials, health workers, social workers, assisting volunteers, or spiritual counselors to protect victims so that they are more sensitive and responsive to the interests of the household which from the outset is directed at the integrity and harmony of the household. To prevent domestic violence, the Regional Government is obliged to carry out duties in the field of women's empowerment to carry out preventive actions, among others, organizing communication, information, and education regarding the prevention of violence against women and children. Based on these considerations, it is time to establish a Regional Regulation that is regulated comprehensively, clearly, and firmly in the implementation of protection of women and children including protection of women and children victims of violence. Article 65

(1) The community participates in assisting prevention and handling efforts for victims of violence and criminal acts against women and children.

(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be realized through actions of providing information and/or reporting the occurrence of violence and criminal acts against women and children to law enforcement or the authorities, or participating in handling victims of violence and criminal acts against women and children.

To realize such integrity and harmony, it is highly dependent on each person within the scope of the household, especially the level of quality of behavior and self-control of each person within the scope of the household. The integrity and harmony of the household can be disrupted if quality and self-control cannot be controlled, which ultimately can result in domestic violence resulting in insecurity or injustice against people within the scope of the household. To prevent, protect victims, and prosecute perpetrators of domestic violence, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and prosecution of perpetrators in accordance with the philosophy of Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state views that all forms of violence, especially domestic violence, are violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of discrimination. The state's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, together with its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to protection of his/her person, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and shall have the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something that is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to obtain facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice". Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence, and domestic neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate domestic violence. The Regional Regulation regulates the matter of prevention and protection as well as recovery for victims of violence, and regulates the obligations of law enforcement officials, health workers, social workers, assisting volunteers, or spiritual counselors to protect victims so that they are more sensitive and responsive to the interests of the household which from the outset is directed at the integrity and harmony of the household. To prevent domestic violence, the Regional Government is obliged to carry out duties in the field of women's empowerment to carry out preventive actions, among others, organizing communication, information, and education regarding the prevention of violence against women and children. Based on these considerations, it is time to establish a Regional Regulation that is regulated comprehensively, clearly, and firmly in the implementation of protection of women and children including protection of women and children victims of violence. CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

The existence of Regional Regulations that side with vulnerable or subordinated groups, particularly women and children, becomes very necessary in connection with the many social problems that result in the deprivation of the human rights of women and children. The human rights of women and children are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child as well as the ratification of the convention on the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, however the enforcement of the human rights of women and children has still not been able to encourage becoming a political commitment in the Region. The form of implementation of protection of women carried out by the Government is to implement gender mainstreaming, namely a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of regional development program policies within the framework of National development. A child is a mandate as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because in him/her is inherent dignity, honor, and rights as a human being that must be upheld. From the perspective of the life of the nation and state, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms. Although Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection has included the rights of children, the implementation of the obligations and responsibilities of parents, family, community, government, and the state to provide protection to children, a Regional Regulation is still needed as a juridical foundation for the implementation of such obligations and responsibilities in the Region. Thus, the establishment of this Regional Regulation is based on the consideration that child protection in all its aspects is part of development activities in the Region, particularly in advancing the life of the nation and state. Parents, family, and community are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise, in the context of implementing child protection, the state and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their growth and development in an optimal and directed manner. This Regional Regulation affirms that the accountability of parents, family, community, Regional Government and the state is a series of activities carried out continuously for the protection of children's rights. This series of activities must be sustainable and directed to ensure the growth and development of children, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially. This action is intended to realize the best life for children who are expected to be potential successors to the nation, resilient, having nationalism imbued with noble character and Pancasila values, as well as having a strong will to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. Child protection efforts need to be implemented as early as possible, namely from the fetus in the womb until the child is 18 (eighteen) years old. Starting from the concept of holistic, comprehensive, and complete child protection, this Regional Regulation places the obligation to provide protection to children based on the following principles:

a. non-discrimination; b. the best interests of the child; c. the right to life, survival, and development; and d. respect for the views of the child. In conducting guidance, development and protection of children, the role of the community is needed, whether through child protection institutions, religious institutions, non-governmental organizations, community organizations, social organizations, business world, mass media, or educational institutions. The form of implementation of child protection carried out by the Regional Government is through mainstreaming children's rights, namely integrating children's issues and rights into every stage of development which includes planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of laws and regulations, policy programs and budgets with the principles of the best interests of the child. The integrity and harmony of a happy, safe, peaceful, and tranquil household is the aspiration of every person in the household. The Republic of Indonesia is a state based on the Belief in the One and Only God as guaranteed by Article 29 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Thus, every person within the scope of the household in carrying out their rights and obligations must be based on religion. This needs to be continuously developed in order to build household integrity.

Regional Government is obliged to implement efforts for the protection of women.

(1) Special protection for child victims of abuse and neglect as referred to in Article 44 is carried out through supervision, prevention, treatment, and rehabilitation by the Regional Government and society.

Article 12

(1) Every child who is deprived of their freedom has the right to: a. receive humane treatment and be placed separately from adults;

b. obtain legal assistance or other assistance effectively at every stage of applicable legal proceedings; and

c. defend themselves and obtain justice before an objective and impartial juvenile court in a closed hearing.

(2) Every child who becomes a victim or perpetrator of sexual violence or who is in conflict with the law has the right to confidentiality.

(1) Every child has the right to obtain protection from being the target of persecution, torture, or imposition of inhuman punishment.

(2) Every child has the right to obtain freedom in accordance with the law.

(3) Arrest, detention, or criminal imprisonment of children shall only be carried out if in accordance with applicable law and can only be carried out as a last resort.

4.2.text: To realize such integrity and harmony, it is highly dependent on each person within the scope of the household, especially the level of quality of behavior and self-control of each person within the scope of the household. The integrity and harmony of the household can be disrupted if quality and self-control cannot be controlled, which ultimately can result in domestic violence resulting in insecurity or injustice against people within the scope of the household. To prevent, protect victims, and prosecute perpetrators of domestic violence, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and prosecution of perpetrators in accordance with the philosophy of Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state views that all forms of violence, especially domestic violence, are violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of discrimination. The state's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, together with its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to protection of his/her person, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and shall have the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something that is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to obtain facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice". Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence, and domestic neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate domestic violence. The Regional Regulation regulates the matter of prevention and protection as well as recovery for victims of violence, and regulates the obligations of law enforcement officials, health workers, social workers, assisting volunteers, or spiritual counselors to protect victims so that they are more sensitive and responsive to the interests of the household which from the outset is directed at the integrity and harmony of the household. To prevent domestic violence, the Regional Government is obliged to carry out duties in the field of women's empowerment to carry out preventive actions, among others, organizing communication, information, and education regarding the prevention of violence against women and children. Based on these considerations, it is time to establish a Regional Regulation that is regulated comprehensively, clearly, and firmly in the implementation of protection of women and children including protection of women and children victims of violence. Article 2

Paragraph (1) Letter a Sufficiently clear. Letter b What is meant by "gender equality" is a condition in which women and men enjoy equal status and have the same conditions to fully realize their basic rights and potential for the integrity and continuity of the household proportionally.

Letter c Sufficiently clear. Letter d Sufficiently clear. Paragraph (2) Letter a Sufficiently clear. Letter b What is meant by "the principle of the best interests of the child" is that in all actions concerning children carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies, and judicial bodies, the best interests of the child must be the primary consideration.

Letter c What is meant by "the principle of the right to life, survival, and development" is the most fundamental basic right of children that is protected by the state, government, society, family, and parents.

Letter d What is meant by "the principle of respect for the views of the child" is respect for the rights of children to participate and express their opinions in decision-making, especially if it concerns matters that affect their lives.
