I. GENERAL

The existence of Regional Regulations that side with vulnerable or subordinated groups, particularly women and children, becomes very necessary in connection with the many social problems that result in the deprivation of the human rights of women and children. The human rights of women and children are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child as well as the ratification of the convention on the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, however the enforcement of the human rights of women and children has still not been able to encourage becoming a political commitment in the Region. The form of implementation of protection of women carried out by the Government is to implement gender mainstreaming, namely a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of regional development program policies within the framework of National development. A child is a mandate as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because in him/her is inherent dignity, honor, and rights as a human being that must be upheld. From the perspective of the life of the nation and state, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms. Although Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection has included the rights of children, the implementation of the obligations and responsibilities of parents, family, community, government, and the state to provide protection to children, a Regional Regulation is still needed as a juridical foundation for the implementation of such obligations and responsibilities in the Region. Thus, the establishment of this Regional Regulation is based on the consideration that child protection in all its aspects is part of development activities in the Region, particularly in advancing the life of the nation and state. Parents, family, and community are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise, in the context of implementing child protection, the state and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their growth and development in an optimal and directed manner. This Regional Regulation affirms that the accountability of parents, family, community, Regional Government and the state is a series of activities carried out continuously for the protection of children's rights. This series of activities must be sustainable and directed to ensure the growth and development of children, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially. This action is intended to realize the best life for children who are expected to be potential successors to the nation, resilient, having nationalism imbued with noble character and Pancasila values, as well as having a strong will to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. Child protection efforts need to be implemented as early as possible, namely from the fetus in the womb until the child is 18 (eighteen) years old. Starting from the concept of holistic, comprehensive, and complete child protection, this Regional Regulation places the obligation to provide protection to children based on the following principles:

a. non-discrimination; b. the best interests of the child; c. the right to life, survival, and development; and d. respect for the views of the child. In conducting guidance, development and protection of children, the role of the community is needed, whether through child protection institutions, religious institutions, non-governmental organizations, community organizations, social organizations, business world, mass media, or educational institutions. The form of implementation of child protection carried out by the Regional Government is through mainstreaming children's rights, namely integrating children's issues and rights into every stage of development which includes planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of laws and regulations, policy programs and budgets with the principles of the best interests of the child. The integrity and harmony of a happy, safe, peaceful, and tranquil household is the aspiration of every person in the household. The Republic of Indonesia is a state based on the Belief in the One and Only God as guaranteed by Article 29 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Thus, every person within the scope of the household in carrying out their rights and obligations must be based on religion. This needs to be continuously developed in order to build household integrity.

Article 29

(1) The Regional Government is obligated to provide facilities and organize comprehensive health efforts for children, so that every child obtains optimal health status from the womb.

(2) The provision of facilities and organization of comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be supported by community participation.

(3) Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) include promotive, preventive, curative, and rehabilitative efforts, both for basic health services and referrals.

(4) Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be organized free of charge for families who are unable to afford them.

(5) The implementation of provisions as referred to in paragraphs (1) through (4) shall be adjusted to the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

(1) The Regional Government is obligated to organize the maintenance and care of neglected children, both within institutions and outside institutions.

(2) The organization of maintenance as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by community institutions. (3) To organize the maintenance and care of neglected children, government institutions and community institutions, as referred to in paragraph (2), may establish cooperation with various related parties.

(4) In the case of organizing maintenance and care as referred to in paragraph (3), its supervision is conducted by regional apparatus institutions that administer social affairs in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

Article 65

(1) The community participates in assisting prevention and handling efforts for victims of violence and criminal acts against women and children.

(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be realized through actions of providing information and/or reporting the occurrence of violence and criminal acts against women and children to law enforcement or the authorities, or participating in handling victims of violence and criminal acts against women and children.

To realize such integrity and harmony, it is highly dependent on each person within the scope of the household, especially the level of quality of behavior and self-control of each person within the scope of the household. The integrity and harmony of the household can be disrupted if quality and self-control cannot be controlled, which ultimately can result in domestic violence resulting in insecurity or injustice against people within the scope of the household. To prevent, protect victims, and prosecute perpetrators of domestic violence, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and prosecution of perpetrators in accordance with the philosophy of Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state views that all forms of violence, especially domestic violence, are violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of discrimination. The state's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, together with its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to protection of his/her person, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and shall have the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something that is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to obtain facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice". Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence, and domestic neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate domestic violence. The Regional Regulation regulates the matter of prevention and protection as well as recovery for victims of violence, and regulates the obligations of law enforcement officials, health workers, social workers, assisting volunteers, or spiritual counselors to protect victims so that they are more sensitive and responsive to the interests of the household which from the outset is directed at the integrity and harmony of the household. To prevent domestic violence, the Regional Government is obliged to carry out duties in the field of women's empowerment to carry out preventive actions, among others, organizing communication, information, and education regarding the prevention of violence against women and children. Based on these considerations, it is time to establish a Regional Regulation that is regulated comprehensively, clearly, and firmly in the implementation of protection of women and children including protection of women and children victims of violence. (1) The Regional Government is obligated to provide facilities and organize comprehensive health efforts for children, so that every child obtains optimal health status from the womb.

(2) The provision of facilities and organization of comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be supported by community participation.

(3) Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) include promotive, preventive, curative, and rehabilitative efforts, both for basic health services and referrals.

(4) Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be organized free of charge for families who are unable to afford them.

(5) The implementation of provisions as referred to in paragraphs (1) through (4) shall be adjusted to the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

The existence of Regional Regulations that side with vulnerable or subordinated groups, particularly women and children, becomes very necessary in connection with the many social problems that result in the deprivation of the human rights of women and children. The human rights of women and children are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child as well as the ratification of the convention on the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, however the enforcement of the human rights of women and children has still not been able to encourage becoming a political commitment in the Region. The form of implementation of protection of women carried out by the Government is to implement gender mainstreaming, namely a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of regional development program policies within the framework of National development. A child is a mandate as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because in him/her is inherent dignity, honor, and rights as a human being that must be upheld. From the perspective of the life of the nation and state, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms. Although Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection has included the rights of children, the implementation of the obligations and responsibilities of parents, family, community, government, and the state to provide protection to children, a Regional Regulation is still needed as a juridical foundation for the implementation of such obligations and responsibilities in the Region. Thus, the establishment of this Regional Regulation is based on the consideration that child protection in all its aspects is part of development activities in the Region, particularly in advancing the life of the nation and state. Parents, family, and community are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise, in the context of implementing child protection, the state and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their growth and development in an optimal and directed manner. This Regional Regulation affirms that the accountability of parents, family, community, Regional Government and the state is a series of activities carried out continuously for the protection of children's rights. This series of activities must be sustainable and directed to ensure the growth and development of children, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially. This action is intended to realize the best life for children who are expected to be potential successors to the nation, resilient, having nationalism imbued with noble character and Pancasila values, as well as having a strong will to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. Child protection efforts need to be implemented as early as possible, namely from the fetus in the womb until the child is 18 (eighteen) years old. Starting from the concept of holistic, comprehensive, and complete child protection, this Regional Regulation places the obligation to provide protection to children based on the following principles:

a. non-discrimination; b. the best interests of the child; c. the right to life, survival, and development; and d. respect for the views of the child. In conducting guidance, development and protection of children, the role of the community is needed, whether through child protection institutions, religious institutions, non-governmental organizations, community organizations, social organizations, business world, mass media, or educational institutions. The form of implementation of child protection carried out by the Regional Government is through mainstreaming children's rights, namely integrating children's issues and rights into every stage of development which includes planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of laws and regulations, policy programs and budgets with the principles of the best interests of the child. The integrity and harmony of a happy, safe, peaceful, and tranquil household is the aspiration of every person in the household. The Republic of Indonesia is a state based on the Belief in the One and Only God as guaranteed by Article 29 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Thus, every person within the scope of the household in carrying out their rights and obligations must be based on religion. This needs to be continuously developed in order to build household integrity.
